notes: Circuit: D9 -> red wire -> R1 (220Ω) -> LED anode; LED cathode -> black wire -> Yún GND, matching the schematic.

The arduino-yun catalogue entry lists its digital pins as the single port 'D0-D13', not as individual pins. 'D9' is therefore not a valid port name. The red wire is attached to 'D0-D13' as the only digital-pin port available. The manual's pin is digital pin 9, between 10~ and 8 on the top header.
The breadboard in the image is a small one drawn rotated, with 5-hole strips running horizontally. Strips are mapped to catalogue columns 10-14 (bank t), top to bottom. This is an assumption.
The LED's bent (longer) leg is the anode. It shares a strip with R1's second leg. The straight leg is the cathode and shares a strip with the black GND wire.
Yún connection to a wireless network and USB power are not drawn in the circuit and are not modelled.

The MCP servers claude.ai Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive need authorization. Authorize them in the claude.ai connector settings. They are unavailable until then, and none of them were needed for this task.
